s.t:
Description
At TripleTen , we're building an international platform of digital re-skilling products to help people from diverse backgrounds learn new professions and build sustainable careers in tech.
Our program graduates have landed jobs at top companies like Tesla, Spotify, PlayStation, Google, and Microsoft. So far, over 5,000 students have chosen TripleTen, and hundreds of new students are joining us each month. We believe everyone can jumpstart a new career, which is why we produce quality educational content and offer intensive courses in tech complete with full access to an interactive platform, code reviews, and support from industry practitioners.
We're launching a program for experienced engineers transitioning into system architecture roles. The curriculum is being built by a team of senior authors. What we need now is the person who brings it to life for students: hosts the live sessions, reviews the work, runs the architecture review boards, and sets the technical bar for the people supporting alongside you.
This is a teaching and review role. You'll be the senior technical presence the cohort learns from week to week. You'll run live sessions and office hours, give real architectural feedback on student deliverables, and act as the escalation point for a team of supporting instructors who handle first-line questions.

The best person for this is someone who has actually designed and shipped systems at scale, has opinions about what good architecture looks like, and can tell an experienced engineer why their design is wrong, not just whether it runs.
Your audience: experienced engineers leveling up to system architecture roles. Many already write production code daily. They will spot shallow feedback instantly, so the bar here is real seniority, not familiarity.
Format: Async-first with scheduled live sessions. Live sessions and office hours are timed around a US-based cohort. Estimated 15 to 25 hrs/week.
Please submit all resumes or CV's in English.

Host weekly live sessions across the program, focused on the design and decision layer: where to split services, how systems scale and fail, which tradeoff to make and why
Run group office hours and 1:1 sessions for students working through projects and the capstone
Review student projects against rubrics: the architecture dossiers, deployed backends, cloud infrastructure, performance reports, security reviews, and the final distributed-system capstone
Give architectural feedback, not just pass/fail checks. Catch when a design decision is unsound, an interface is wrong, or a scope is unrealistic, and explain the better path
Run the mock architecture review boards and the simulated executive-panel presentations, and give structured, senior-level critique
Set the technical standard for a team of supporting instructors who cover questions and first-line review, and act as their escalation point on design and architecture calls

5+ years as a senior software/systems architect, platform engineer, or senior backend/infrastructure engineer
Has designed and shipped systems at scale in a real company, not just coursework or side projects
Depth across the architectural spine: system design, API and service architecture, cloud and infrastructure (AWS, Kubernetes, Terraform, CI/CD), and distributed systems
Can explain why a decision was made, not just how it was implemented, and can diagnose and critique someone else's architecture live
Strong technical communication: comfortable leading a live session and writing clear, specific review feedback
Strong English C1+ — instruction and review are in English for a US-based audience
Comfortable using AI tools in day-to-day technical work
What we can offer you
Milestone-based payments tied to deliverables
Fully remote work with flexible hours
A digital office — we use modern tools (Notion, Miro, Slack, Figma) to keep collaboration smooth
Professional trust and autonomy — no micromanaging
The chance to see real impact: our metric is graduates landing jobs in tech
Join a diverse, international, and close-knit team excited to work with you

Job Summary: The Office of the Chief Administrative Officer (CAO) provides operations support services and business solutions to the community of 10,000 House Members, Officers and staff.

The CAO organization comprises more than 800 technical and administrative staff working in a variety of areas, including information technology, finance, budget management, human resources, payroll, child care, food and vending, procurement, logistics and administrative counsel.

This position is located in the Network Engineering and Operations (Networking) Directorate, House Information Resources (HIR), Office of the Chief Administrative Officer (CAO), U.S. House of Representatives (House).

The Networking Directorate provides operational support services to the House that ensure reliable and dependable connectivity to the House Data Network both on the House Campus and to over 820 District Offices as well as numerous Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery (BC/DR) sites, facilities, and mobile capabilities.

This position does not have day-today supervisory/managerial responsibilities. Primary Responsibilities: Evaluates and recommends commercially available, standards compliant LAN networking solutions.

Design, test, and implement new LAN deployments and upgrades based on project requirements Designs complex integrated communication networks and develops network service specifications and procedures. Provides operational support on day‐to‐day operations and resolution to complex LAN, WAN, Wireless and ISE related problems.

Assists in the preparation of Request for Proposals and Request for Quotations. Reviews and evaluates reliable, cost‐effective, and efficient campus LAN communications for the House. Conducts performance and bandwidth utilization monitoring of LAN communication systems.

Keeps abreast of relevant routing and switching technology changes and applies industry standards to House requirements. Trains other House staff in telecommunications technologies and provides technical guidance to junior level engineers. Performs other official duties and special projects as assigned.
Qualifications: Minimum Qualifications: Bachelor’s degree in a related field or equivalent work experience. Minimum 5 years of experience designing and supporting large scale campus LAN/ WAN and wireless networks. Knowledge of TCP, UDP, QoS, SNMP, TLS/HTTPS, SMTP, EIGRP, OSPF, and BGP.

Experience with Aruba wireless access hardware ideal but not required. Demonstrate proficiency with managing large scale enterprise networks using Cisco’s routing and switching best practices.

Strong understanding of how to configure access ports and trunk ports Knowledge of port security and how to define violation modes on layer 2 access points Proficient in using design tools such as Visio to road map the enterprise infrastructure. Skill in the coordination of network engineering and integration projects.

Knowledge, Skill, and Ability (KSA) and Competency Requirements: Ability to provide engineering leadership on all phases of analysis, design, testing, and implementation of networks, integration of voice and data, and telecommunications.

Ability to communicate effectively, both orally and in writing, with elected officials, senior staff, information systems professional, and non-technical users.

Employees within this position are expected to demonstrate the following IHR Technical Competencies: Analytics; Application Administration and Integration; Emergency Response Planning and Risk Management; Hardware Installation and Management; Information Management; Information Resources Strategy and Planning; Information Systems/Network Security; Information Technology Support; Knowledge of Emerging Trends and Industry Best Practices; Network Management; Project Management; Quality Assurance and Testing; and Telecommunications.

All employees within CAO are expected to demonstrate the following general competencies: Accountability, Adaptability, Collaboration, Communication, Customer Orientation, Knowledge of Relevant Policies, Procedures, and Processes, Priority Management, and Problem Resolution. Certifications: CCNA or CCNP preferred.

Continued employment is contingent upon satisfactorily completing a criminal history records check (or other applicable security clearance) and a pre-employment drug-test (pre-identified position only).

This is an exciting role at Zapier in a growing team, and you will play a direct role in implementing and improving Zapier's IT infrastructure. Working closely with our Engineering, People Ops, and Security Teams, you will implement, manage, automate, and support the tools and services that power a globally distributed team.
We believe that a good IT experience is a perk -- it keeps people productive and engaged rather than getting in the way. You will help maintain a world-class Mac experience for our employees and streamline access management by implementing SSO applications and automating processes.

You will help scale our IT infrastructure and processes to the next level as a service owner, and you will be crucial to its success as Zapier grows. This isn't an IT Helpdesk job, but assisting and providing great customer service for Zapier's IT needs is part of the role.

Responsibilities Peraton is seeking a highly experienced Okta IAM/Identity Integration Engineer to support the Department of Defense's next-generation enterprise Identity, Credential, and Access Management (ICAM) platform that is replacing DS Logon and providing secure authentication services for millions of Service Members, Veterans, Family Members, and Beneficiaries.

The Alternative Multi-factor Authentication Support Services (AMASS) Program provides secure, scalable identity and access management services across the Department of Defense, enabling authentication, authorization, and digital identity interoperability for high‑visibility DoD systems.

In this role, you will design, integrate, and sustain identity services using the Okta Identity Engine (OIE), implement secure authentication flows using the Okta Embedded SDK, and ensure compliance with DoD cybersecurity policies, including RMF, STIG, and NIST guidelines.

This position requires extensive hands‑on experience with modern identity protocols, mobile authentication, and enterprise IAM/ICAM solutions within Federal environments. This is a 100% remote role. Responsibilities Configure, administer, and optimize Okta Identity Engine (OIE) to support DoD enterprise identity workflows.

Implement and support the Okta Embedded SDK to deliver secure and standardized authentication for partner applications. Develop and enhance mobile identity integrations for native iOS and Android platforms supporting DoD mission applications. Implement modern identity standards including OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect (OIDC), and PKCE.

Configure phishing‑resistant authentication methods, including FIDO2/WebAuthn, in alignment with DoD Zero Trust objectives. Design and maintain adaptive and risk-based authentication policies. Integrate identity federation services (OIDC, SAML 2.0) including external Identity Provider (IdP) connections.

Manage authentication token lifecycles (JWT, ID, Access, Refresh tokens) across DoD application ecosystems. Implement secure API authentication using OAuth scopes, claims, and structured authorization patterns. Build identity automation using Okta Workflows and no‑code/low‑code orchestration tooling.

Integrate Okta with DoD authoritative data sources and enterprise-level IAM services. Evaluate and document multiple Okta Mobile implementation alternatives and contribute to the Government Analysis of Alternatives (AoA). Design headless authentication architectures supporting embedded mobile authentication.

Design reusable authentication services supporting multiple relying-party mobile applications. Design secure device-bound credential registration and provisioning. Support Configuration Control Board (CCB) reviews and technical architecture presentations. Design alternative MFA pathways for users without CAC credentials.

Design proxy authentication capabilities supporting beneficiary relationships. Support identity lifecycle processes, including provisioning, deprovisioning, profile management, and attribute governance. Troubleshoot complex identity, federation, and mobile SDK integration issues across multiproduct DoD environments.

Utilize REST APIs, Postman, and related tooling for API development, testing, and validation. Work with DevSecOps teams to integrate IAM capabilities into CI/CD pipelines supporting DoD modernization. Ensure identity implementations comply with DoD RMF, DISA STIGs, NIST SP 800‑63, and other Federal cybersecurity mandates.

Our DNS squad runs the naming, addressing and time services the rest of the internet quietly assumes will always be there: authoritative and recursive DNS, DHCP, forward proxy and NTP, together with the IP address management that ties them together. Our authoritative platform serves roughly 20 million zones from 12 anycast locations across two autonomous systems . Our DNS/DHCP/IPAM management system, DIM, is open source (github.com/ionos-core/dim) - what we build here, others run too.
Tasks

Operate, harden and evolve our authoritative and recursive DNS, DHCP, forward-proxy, DNS and IP Management (DIM) and NTP services so they stay boringly reliable at internet scale.
Automate everything that should be automated - infrastructure as code in Puppet, reviewed and version-controlled - and remove the toil that does not need a human.
Instrument and measure: build the metrics, dashboards and signals that tell us what our services are actually doing, because we cannot improve what we cannot see.
Drive root-cause analysis and lasting fixes through structured ITIL Incident, Problem, Risk and Change management - we make our work and our challenges transparent on purpose.
Take part in the team's on-call rotation for this KRITIS/NIS2 infrastructure (your turn comes up roughly once a month - mandatory and separately compensated) and use what you learn on-call to make the next on-call quieter.

Tools of the Trade
You will work with the protocol implementations and the tooling we use to deliver these services and keep them stable:
DNS / DHCP / proxy / time: PowerDNS (authoritative, recursor, dnsdist), ISC DHCP (experience with or appetite for Kea is welcome), Squid, chrony.
Platform & automation: Enterprise Linux 9, Puppet (GitOps), BIRD, rsyslog, collectd.
Languages: Python, Go, Java, Bash — plus the classic unix toolbelt (awk, sed, git) that still does more than people expect.
Data: ClickHouse, MariaDB, PostgreSQL.
You do not need to have mastered all of these on day one. You do need to be the kind of engineer who is comfortable reaching for the right one and going deep when it matters.

We care less about a perfect CV than about how you think. We work by a few principles, and we mean them:
"If you can't measure it, you can't improve it." We make data-driven decisions and monitor continuously.
"Do it once, do it right." Quality and attention to detail matter to us - shortcuts come back as incidents.
"Perfection is achieved not when there is nothing more to add, but when there is nothing left to take away." We strive for simplicity and efficiency in every solution; the best fix is often the one that deletes complexity.

Have operated DNS, DHCP or comparable network services in production, ideally at scale and under real reliability obligations.
Read RFCs for fun, debug with packet captures, and are not satisfied by "it works again" without knowing why it broke.
Automate by default and treat configuration as code.
Bring radical candor - say the uncomfortable thing early, in service of the work, not the ego.
Think in terms of blast radius. We use AI-assisted tooling in our development and test workflow, but production changes are always human-gated - risk awareness is a feature, not a brake.
If you have ever caused (or narrowly avoided) an interesting outage and learned something durable from it, tell us about it. That is operational experience, not a red flag.

We are building a full-stack AI cloud platform that supports developers and enterprises from data and model training through to production deployment, without the cost and complexity of building large in-house AI/ML infrastructure.

The VPC (Virtual Private Cloud) team builds and operates the core networking layer of our cloud platform. We enable virtual machines to communicate reliably by abstracting them from the underlying physical network, providing seamless IP-based connectivity even as workloads move across the datacenter.
Our team designs secure, isolated private networks for customers, connects them to the public internet, and delivers essential networking services such as load balancers, firewalls, and security groups. Because nearly every cloud application depends on networking, VPC is a foundational service for the entire platform.
Stability and resilience are our top priorities—we engineer systems to remain reliable and operational even when parts of the cloud experience failures.

Junior Space Systems Engineer
Location: London, UK (on-site, Borough / London Bridge)
Type: Full-time
Level: Junior / early-career - ideal for someone coming off a graduate scheme, though exceptional recent graduates with strong project experience are very welcome
Compensation: £35,000–£45,000 depending on experience, plus meaningful equity through our government-backed EMI scheme
_____
We are Foundational
We're an early-stage, mission-driven startup tackling one of the hardest and most exciting engineering challenges in the space domain: building the most precise understanding of space and Earth using ground-based lasers.
Using satellite laser ranging (SLR) and space debris laser ranging (SDLR) data, we're giving the next generation of space companies exquisite orbital data - the foundation for resilient navigation, Earth observation, and precise space traffic control. This is essential infrastructure for the sustainability and resilience of the space domain, and we think it will be foundational to the future economy.
Our network doesn't stop at the ground. To close the loop on precision, we're building the small optical payloads that fly on-orbit and talk back to our stations, and the systems engineering that ties ground, space, and data platform into one coherent whole. That's where you come in.

This is a hands-on engineering role where the successful candidate will be as happy working in the lab as they are behind a computer. You'll work in our space team but may get involved in ground systems as well - helping to define what we build, model it, then get hands-on to build, test, and prove it.
You'll see the full lifecycle: early concept and trade studies, through modelling and design, into integration, environmental test, and validation against our ground network. It's physics-first, hands-on work with a quick path from your bench to orbit. You'll sit in a small team of software and hardware engineers who don't draw hard lines between disciplines, and you'll be expected to cross those lines too.

Systems engineering. Turning mission needs into requirements, interfaces, and budgets (mass, power, link, pointing, timing, error). Running trade studies and making the case for a design decision with numbers behind it.
Modelling & analysis. Building performance models - radiometry and link budgets, atmospheric transmission, pointing and attitude, detection probability - and using them to drive real design choices rather than to decorate them.
Design & build. Contributing to the design of small space-based payloads and ground subsystems: component selection, layout, tolerancing, and assembly of hardware and optical benches alongside our senior engineers.
Integration, test & verification. Assembling and aligning hardware, then putting it through environmental qualification (thermal, vibration, vacuum) and performance characterisation - and learning first-hand what survives launch.
Ground-to-space validation. Working with the ground systems team to validate ranging precision and pointing accuracy end-to-end, so the payload and the network behave as one system.
Owning your corner. Documenting designs, feeding lessons into the next iteration, and taking real responsibility for a slice of the system as we grow.

You don't need flight heritage or a decade of experience. We care far more about strong fundamentals, hunger, and the ability to learn fast in a hands-on environment.
Essential
A degree in space systems engineering, aerospace or mechanical or electrical engineering, physics, or a closely related field.
Strong engineering and physics fundamentals, and the instinct to reach for a first-principles estimate before an opinion.
Some practical engineering experience - a graduate scheme, internship, placement year, or a serious university project or competition team. What matters is that you've built something real and dealt with the consequences.
Hands-on instincts. You like building, aligning, breaking, and fixing hardware, not only simulating it.
Scripting ability for analysis and modelling (Python preferred; MATLAB or similar is fine).
Comfort with ambiguity and ownership. You're energised by a startup where scope is broad, priorities shift, and nobody hands you a fully-specified task list.
Clear communication and a collaborative, low-ego approach to working across software and hardware.
The right to work in the UK.

Hands-on experience with space hardware: CubeSats or smallsats, optical ground stations, LiDAR, or laser systems. Academic projects and competitions absolutely count.
Familiarity with orbital mechanics and the formats that go with it (TLEs, CPF/CRD).

s.h: Exposure to environmental or space qualification testing.
s.t:
Optics fundamentals - geometrical and physical optics, radiometry, detectors and laser sources - or exposure to optical design software (Zemax, Code V).
Comfort in Linux environments, or experience writing instrument control and data-analysis code.
Awareness of laser safety standards (e.g. BS EN 60825).
FPGA or embedded work, particularly for timing applications.
Why Foundational
Real ownership. A high-impact role with genuine autonomy in a new startup - your contributions directly shape our product and our success.
Cutting-edge work. Meaningful, challenging, complex problems at the frontier of the space domain.
Equity that matters. Government-backed EMI scheme options in a fast-growing, VC-backed company.
A team worth learning from. A dynamic, collaborative environment built on innovation, creativity, and teamwork - with room to grow fast.
A mission you can believe in. What we build underpins the future of Earth observation and space traffic control.
Foundational is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and are committed to building an inclusive team.

The objective of this initiative is to establish and grow a centralized pool of space engineering expertise within ETH Zurich | Space. This pool supports ETH Zurich-led space projects and technology programs, strengthening ETH Zurich’s role in the Swiss and international space ecosystem.
The Flight Software Systems Engineer will support a diverse portfolio of small spacecraft, scientific instruments, robotic systems, and technology demonstrators. The work includes resource-constrained missions, integration with externally supplied spacecraft platforms, autonomous functions, and future distributed or coordinated spacecraft concepts.

This role interfaces across systems engineering, avionics, payloads, and software development, and coordinates with external platform providers and mission operations teams.
Aufgaben-/Stellenbeschreibung
As part of the specialized resource pool, you will provide flight software and software systems engineering expertise across multiple ETH Zurich space projects. You will contribute from early mission formulation and software architecture through implementation, integration, verification, launch preparation, and operations.

s.h: As part of your role, you will
s.t:
Take technical ownership of assigned flight software developments and act as the primary software interface to systems engineering, avionics, payload teams, mission operations, and external platform providers.
Translate mission concept of operations into spacecraft behaviors and define flight software architectures and functional decompositions
Allocate hardware-software functions, and define associated software requirements and interfaces.
Translate mission and system requirements into software specifications, interface control documents, operational concepts, and verification plans.
Develop embedded flight software in C and C++ and supporting tools and test scripts (e.g., Python), including device drivers, telemetry and telecommand handling, onboard data management, application software, and fault-management functions.
Integrate flight software with onboard computers, sensors, actuators, payload electronics, communication interfaces, ground systems, and externally supplied spacecraft platforms.
Set up and maintain flat-sat flight software testbeds
Perform software-related trade studies covering processing capacity, memory, timing, bandwidth, autonomy, reliability, and fault tolerance.
Develop real-time, event-driven, autonomous, synchronization, and GNC-related software functions where required.
Establish and maintain software baselines, configuration control, versioning, build automation, continuous integration, release management, and requirements traceability.
Develop and execute flight software unit tests, conduct integration, software-in-the-loop, processor-in-the-loop, hardware-in-the-loop, and system-level verification and validation activities.
Support software risk management, anomaly investigation, non-conformance handling, and technical review boards.
Support spacecraft and payload assembly, integration, and test activities, commissioning, in-flight software updates, telemetry analysis, and mission operations.
Contribute to technical reviews, early-stage mission concepts, proposals, and software feasibility studies.
Provide technical guidance to junior engineers, researchers, and student teams.
Ihr Profil
You have a strong background in embedded and real-time software development combined with systems-level experience in software architecture, requirements engineering, interface definition, integration, and functional verification. You are comfortable working across mission, spacecraft, avionics, payload, software, and operations domains.

s.h: We are looking for someone with
s.t:
Master’s degree in computer science, electrical engineering, computer engineering, aerospace engineering, robotics, or a related field.
5+ years of professional experience in flight software, embedded software, or mission-critical software systems.
Strong programming skills in C and C++ for resource-constrained embedded targets.
Experience with real-time operating systems, embedded Linux, or bare-metal development.
Experience in software systems engineering, including architecture definition, functional decomposition, hardware-software allocation, requirements management, and interface control.
Ability to translate mission and spacecraft requirements into software specifications, operational concepts, and verification strategies.
Experience integrating flight software with avionics hardware, sensors, actuators, communication buses, payloads, or ground systems.
Understanding of telemetry and telecommand, onboard data handling, timing, autonomy, fault management, and spacecraft operations.
Hands-on experience with software integration, debugging, automated testing, and hardware-in-the-loop environments.
Experience with configuration management, version control, release processes, technical baselines, and requirements traceability.
Ability to assess software-related technical resources, including processing capacity, memory, timing, bandwidth, and reliability margins.
Strong analytical, organizational, and communication skills, with the ability to work effectively in multidisciplinary and multicultural teams.
Knowledge of radiation effects, redundancy, memory protection, watchdogs, and FDIR.
Excellent command of English, both written and spoken; German is an advantage but not required.

s.h: Additionally, the following characteristics are a plus
s.t:
Experience developing flight software for CubeSats, small satellites, scientific instruments, planetary systems, or Class D/Gamma-type missions.
Experience leading or coordinating software-related and functional AIT activities, including test planning, execution, anomaly resolution, and system-level functional verification.
Experience integrating payload software with spacecraft platforms supplied by external industrial partners.
Familiarity with ECSS software engineering and software product assurance standards, NASA software practices, or comparable development frameworks.
Experience with spacecraft protocols and buses such as SpaceWire, CAN, UART, SPI, I²C, Ethernet, or CCSDS-based services.
Experience with flight software frameworks or operating systems such as NASA cFS, F Prime, RTEMS, FreeRTOS, Zephyr, or equivalent.
Experience with autonomous systems, robotic software, relative navigation, formation flying, or distributed spacecraft coordination.
Experience with FPGA or firmware interfaces and hardware-software co-design.
Experience with EGSE, simulators, ground software, commissioning, or in-orbit operations.
Experience collaborating with international partners, space agencies, research institutions, or spacecraft suppliers.
